mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo engine replacement typically costs £2,500-£5,200 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitting adding £800-£1,500 depending on the workshop. Used engines: £1,500-£3,500 depending on code and condition. Reconditioned: £2,500-£4,200. Rebuilt: £3,200-£5,200. Full supply & fit: £3,300-£6,700 total.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most critical and preventable failure is timing belt failure - the F4R engine requires a belt change every 72,000 miles / 72 months. If the belt breaks, valve damage is highly likely. Other common issues include turbocharger wear (especially wastegate rattle and sticking), boost control solenoid failure, ignition coil failure, and oil consumption on higher-mileage examples.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and condition. A standard Megane RS 225/250 is worth £4,000-£12,000; R26.R and 275 Trophy examples can exceed £18,000. If the car is worth under £5,000 and needs a full engine replacement, carefully evaluate against scrap value. If the car is worth £6,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine (£2,500-£5,200) is usually financially viable. If the timing belt has failed but the engine block is intact, a cylinder head repair (£1,000-£1,800) may be the most cost-effective solution.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo engine replacement takes 2-4 days for a specialist workshop. Timing belt replacement: 6-10 hours labour. Turbo replacement: 5-8 hours labour. Full engine swap: 12-18 hours due to the tight engine bay and performance component integration. Supply & fit lead time: 5-10 working days from quote acceptance to completion.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between F4R 774, F4R 874 and F4R 876 in the Megane RS?

acceptedAnswer.text: These are different power output variants of the same F4R turbo engine family. F4R 774 / F4Rt 774: 225-230 hp - found in Megane II RS (2004-2009). F4R 874: 250 hp - found in Megane III RS (2009-2012). F4R 876 / 877 / 878 / 879: 265-275 hp - found in Megane III RS 265/275 (2012-2016). All share the same cast-iron block and basic architecture, but with different turbocharger calibrations, ECU maps, and some internal upgrades. historyTimeline.h2: Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo, powered by the F4R engine family, was introduced in 2004 and remained in production across three Megane generations until 2023. The F4R is a cast-iron block, 16-valve DOHC turbocharged engine derived from the naturally aspirated F4R unit, with a reinforced connecting rod and piston group, revised camshafts, and a TwinScroll MHI TD04 turbocharger. From 225 hp in the Megane II RS through to 275 hp in the Megane III RS, the F4R became one of the most celebrated hot hatch engines of its era - robust, tuneable and, when maintained, remarkably reliable.

milestones.description: Megane II Renaultsport 225 launched; F4R 774 / F4Rt 774, 2.0-litre turbo, 225 hp, 300 Nm torque
R26 limited edition; 230 hp version of F4R
Megane III Renaultsport launched; F4R 874, 250 hp, 340 Nm torque
Megane III RS facelift; updated F4R 876/877/878 variants
Megane IV RS launched; new 1.8-litre turbo engine (M5P) replaces F4R
2023 - Megane IV RS continues with 1.8 TCe engine

commonProblems.h2: Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo's F4R engine is fundamentally robust and, when properly maintained, capable of covering over 250,000-300,000 kilometres without major repairs. However, several well-documented issues can lead to significant repair bills - and in some cases, a full engine replacement is the most cost-effective solution. The F4R 774 and F4R 874 codes dominate replacement demand for the Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Belt Failure - The F4R's Critical Service Item
problems.affectedModels: Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo (all F4R codes, 2004-2016)
problems.rootCause: The F4R uses a belt-driven timing system that requires replacement at regular intervals. If the belt breaks, valves can bend, requiring head removal and valve replacement. Unlike some engines with "free-running" designs, the F4R can suffer serious damage if the belt fails - though some sources note special piston recesses may limit damage. The crank pulley is also a known weak point and should be replaced with the belt.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full belt kit with tensioner, idler, water pump and crank pulley
repairOptions.longevity: Best value; prevents catastrophic failure; essential every 72,000 miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Head removal, valve replacement, head skimming and refitting
repairOptions.longevity: If belt has snapped but bottom end is intact
When belt failure has caused bottom-end damage or multiple components have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo (2004-2016) sits in the £4,000-£18,000 range depending on generation, mileage and condition. R26.R and 275 Trophy examples command significant premiums. For standard 225/250 models worth under £6,000, a full engine replacement may approach the vehicle's value. A preventative timing belt replacement (£550-£900) is always excellent value and should be the first priority for any RS owner.
problems.recommendation: If your Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo is approaching 72,000 miles or the belt hasn't been changed in 5+ years, have the timing belt, water pump, tensioner and crank pulley replaced immediately. This is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. If the belt has already snapped, a specialist cylinder head repair may be viable - but carefully evaluate the condition of the bottom end before committing. If the engine has suffered catastrophic failure, a rebuilt unit through EnginesMarket is the cost-effective route - warranty included.

problems.h4: Turbocharger & Boost Control Issues - Wastegate Rattle and Loss of Power
problems.affectedModels: Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo (all F4R codes, higher-mileage examples)
problems.rootCause: The F4R engine's MHI TD04 turbocharger is a known weak point - the turbine typically runs normally up to about 150,000 km (93,000 miles), after which radial rotor play often develops and it can start pushing oil into the exhaust. The 2.0T (F4R) in the Megane RS is also known for wastegate rattle and eventual sticking, caused by carbon buildup or a seized actuator. Boost control solenoid failure is another common cause of overboost or underboost conditions.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New wastegate actuator or boost control solenoid
repairOptions.longevity: If wastegate is sticking or solenoid has failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Reconditioned or new turbo unit with oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo has developed play, oil leaks or boost issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Rebuilt engine with new turbo and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo examples under £6,000, turbo replacement (£800-£1,600) is usually viable if the rest of the car is sound. If the turbo failure has sent debris through the engine, a full replacement may be the only safe option - and may push repair costs beyond vehicle value on older examples.
problems.recommendation: If you experience a whistling turbo that sounds like a siren, loss of power, or a check engine light with boost-related codes, have the turbo and boost control system inspected promptly. Addressing wastegate or solenoid issues early can prevent turbo failure. Ensure oil feed lines are clean and free from restriction - oil starvation is a common cause of turbo failure on the F4R.

problems.group: Oil Consumption, Ignition Coils & Lambda Sensors
problems.h4: Oil Consumption, Ignition Coils & Lambda Sensors - High-Mileage Wear Items
problems.affectedModels: Renault Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo (all F4R codes, 80,000+ miles)
problems.rootCause: After 150,000 km, oil consumption of about 1 litre per 1,000 km is not uncommon - typically caused by stuck piston rings or hardened valve stem seals. Ignition coils and lambda sensors are also known weak points at higher mileage. Cold-start misfires often point to coil pack issues.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New genuine or OEM-quality coil packs

repairOptions.longevity: If engine warning light relates to emissions

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Piston rings, valve stem seals, full top-end rebuild
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is excessive and other options exhausted

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For Megane Renaultsport 2.0 Turbo examples under £5,000, coil pack or lambda replacement (£150-£300) is a minor expense. Full engine rebuild for oil consumption should be carefully evaluated against the vehicle's value and overall condition.
problems.recommendation: Regular oil changes (every 10,000 km or 1 year) using the correct 5W-40 (RN0710) oil is essential for F4R longevity. If you experience misfires, start with coil pack inspection and replacement - this is the cheapest and most common fix. For oil consumption, monitor usage carefully; if it exceeds 1 litre per 1,000 km, a professional inspection is recommended.
